company: German Green Steel and Power Limited

summary.one_line: German Green Steel and Power is a Gujarat-focused maker of secondary-route TMT bars that is growing and fairly well run operationally. It is raising Rs.290 crore mostly for a sensible capacity expansion, but it has no real moat, 98% of its sales are in one state, it does not own its brand, and there are live governance issues: a Rs.112.65 crore income-tax contingent liability after a 2023 search, a web of promoter entities, and recent compliance penalties. We would avoid it for now.
bull_points: Growth has been real, and FY26 was organic. Revenue grew from Rs.1,129.78 crore in FY24 to Rs.1,678.98 crore in FY26. The EBITDA margin widened from 7.02% to 9.94%, and PAT rose from Rs.41.67 crore to Rs.79.89 crore (S1, p.298, 391).

Most of the money goes into the business: 97% of the Rs.303.90 crore issue is fresh money (Rs.290 crore). Rs.226.33 crore of it funds capex, and the OFS is only 10 lakh shares, about Rs.13.9 crore (S1, p.138; S6).
The expansion is backed by demand. Combined TMT utilisation was 87.79% and sponge iron 95.21% in FY26, and the plan roughly doubles Samakhiyali's billet and TMT capacity (S1, p.305, 309-310).

Captive power keeps costs down. The Samakhiyali plant got 75.44% of its FY26 power from its own 20 MW captive plant, and group-wide grid dependence fell from 61.68% in FY24 to 33.02% in FY26 (S1, p.300, 315-316).
The balance sheet has de-levered. Debt-to-equity fell from 1.18 in FY25 to 0.79 in FY26, and operating cash flow nearly doubled to Rs.140.80 crore (S1, p.394, 436; S6).
bear_points: There is no moat. This is commodity rebar made by the induction-furnace route, and CARE says Gujarat added 68 steel units in five years, creating overcapacity. 97.74% of FY26 sales were in Gujarat (S1, p.304; S2, p.242).

The company does not own its brand. The 'German TMT' mark belongs to promoter-group firm Haq Steels Pvt Ltd and is licensed on a non-exclusive royalty basis. The quenching technology licence (Thermex, from H&K) is renewed year by year after a cease-and-desist dispute (S1, p.304-305, 342-343, 480-481).

Income-tax contingent liabilities rose to Rs.112.65 crore at March 2026, from nil in FY24, after a January 2023 search covering the company, promoters and group companies. That is about 27% of net worth. The promoters personally face 12 direct-tax cases totalling Rs.30.60 crore (S1, p.83, 63, 482).

Working capital is financed through suppliers. Trade payables of Rs.329.54 crore include Rs.242.90 crore under a supplier-financing arrangement, which is effectively bank credit sitting outside reported borrowings of Rs.334.37 crore (S1, p.390, 425, 475).

The related-party web is dense and still growing. FY26 includes sales to four Kaavyaratna LLPs, receivables of Rs.20.6 crore from them, and a Rs.6.90 crore capital advance to one. Purchases from Iraki Enterprise were Rs.62.30 crore, and there are leases from three promoter entities (S1, p.84-88, 437-441).
watch_points: Whether the expansion is delivered on time. Commercial production is now scheduled for December 2027, pushed back from October 2026 in the DRHP, and parts of the kiln package are still unordered (S1, p.166-168; S2, p.147).
How the income-tax appeals arising from the 2023 search turn out, given the Rs.112.65 crore contingent liability (S1, p.63, 83).

Whether the company can grow outside Gujarat (Rajasthan, Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh), and what the JSW One contract-manufacturing deal actually earns, since no revenue figure has been disclosed (S1, p.304-306, 342).
Final subscription by category at close on 29 September. Day-1 figures were not yet meaningful when this was written (S13).

reasoning: The use of the money is the strongest part of the case, but not enough on its own. Rs.226.33 crore of the Rs.290 crore fresh issue funds a capacity expansion that current utilisation justifies (87.79% TMT, 95.21% sponge iron). However, commercial production is now expected only in December 2027, the target has already slipped about 14 months since the DRHP, and the project cost has risen from Rs.325.21 crore to Rs.348.14 crore (S1, p.138-140, 166, 309; S2, p.133, 147).

There is no durable competitive advantage to earn a premium over time. The product is BIS-standard TMT sold almost entirely in Gujarat, a state CARE describes as over-capacitised. The company's roughly 3 lakh tonne TMT capacity is under 1% of India's 50.3 MT TMT market (our calculation). Its brand belongs to a promoter-group company and its rolling technology is licensed yearly from a party that sent it a cease-and-desist (S1, p.304, 342-343, 480; S2, p.206, 242, 247).

The growth is genuine but lower quality than the headline suggests. FY25 revenue growth of 33% came mainly from consolidating German TMT, a Viramgam unit bought in 2024 from a promoter-family-controlled position, and it contributed Rs.30.15 crore of FY26 PAT. Organic FY26 growth was 11.4%. Margins are thin (4.76% PAT), and free cash flow was deeply negative in FY24 and FY25 (S1, p.435, 460-467, 394).

Governance flags stack up across several areas at once, not just one:
  - Income-tax contingent liability of Rs.112.65 crore after a group-wide search, plus Rs.30.60 crore of direct-tax cases against the promoters.
  - Penalties paid in December 2025 for running without an audit committee, an NRC, independent directors and a woman director.
  - Company-secretary turnover: the CS resigned in July 2026, two months before the issue.
  - A growing ring of promoter-linked entities on both the buy and sell side (S1, p.63, 83, 84-88, 356, 367-369, 482; S2, p.66-68).

The balance sheet is less comfortable than the 0.79 debt-to-equity ratio implies. Rs.242.90 crore of supplier-financed payables, a current ratio of 0.97 and personal promoter guarantees across almost every facility make the business sensitive to a steel-price or credit downturn (S1, p.425, 436, 444-448).

What would change the call: a clean outcome on the tax appeals, on-time commissioning of the expanded plant, the 'German TMT' mark transferred into the listed company, and the related-party ring shrinking. Until then, a retail investor takes promoter and tax risk that the business's modest margins do not compensate for (S1, p.63, 166, 304).

subsections.title: What the company makes and how it earns

blocks.text: German Green Steel and Power Limited (GGSPL) was incorporated in 2008 as Haq Enterprises Pvt Ltd. It was renamed Haq Steels and Metaliks, then German Green Steel and Power in January 2024 (S1, p.336). It is a vertically integrated iron and steel maker. At Samakhiyali, Kutch, it turns iron ore and coal into sponge iron (DRI) in a rotary kiln. That sponge iron is melted with purchased scrap in induction furnaces and cast into MS billets, and the billets are rolled into TMT reinforcement bars (8-40 mm, Fe500 to Fe550D and CRS grades) using a licensed Thermex quenching process (S1, p.297-298, 313-315; S16).

TMT bars are now the business: 78.74% of FY26 revenue, up from 63.13% in FY24. MS billets and sponge iron are mostly consumed internally, and only the surplus is sold. Around 90% of billets and 73% of sponge iron were used captively in FY26. 'Others' are mainly by-products and traded scrap such as mill scale and fly ash (S1, p.298, 306, 311).

blocks.caption: Revenue by product (Rs. lakh; % of revenue) (S1, p.298, 306)

blocks.text: Pricing is spot and commodity-linked. There are no long-term sales contracts. Products are sold on purchase orders on a free-on-road basis, and raw-material prices track international scrap and ore prices (S1, p.313, 316-318). The company therefore earns a conversion spread over scrap and ore, and its captive power lowers the cost side. Management also flags weaker demand in the monsoon (S1, p.456-457).

The 'German TMT' brand under which almost everything is sold is owned by Haq Steels Pvt Ltd, a promoter-group company. It is licensed to GGSPL and its subsidiary under a non-exclusive 10-year royalty agreement dated 3 March 2025 for Rs.6 lakh a year each, rising 10% a year. GGSPL's only registered trademark is its slogan (S1, p.304-305, 342).

There are two plants, both in Gujarat. Samakhiyali (Kutch) covers about 5.75 lakh sq m of owned land, about 105 km from Mundra and 50 km from Kandla ports. It was bought in 2018 for Rs.35.70 crore through the IBC liquidation of New Tech Forge and Foundry (S1, p.299, 336-340). Viramgam (Ahmedabad district) belongs to the 97.41%-owned subsidiary German TMT Pvt Ltd (formerly German TMX), which GGSPL acquired in 2024. That plant makes billets and TMT only and has no DRI (S1, p.308, 435).

blocks.caption: Installed capacity and utilisation, certified by Multi Engineers, 5 Sep 2026 (S1, p.309-310)

blocks.text:
Power is the most real cost advantage the company has:
- At Samakhiyali it owns a 16 MW coal-based captive plant and a 4 MW waste-heat-recovery plant, which runs on kiln flue gas.
- It has leased or part-owned wind and solar capacity at Bhavnagar (8.1 MW wind, 6 MW DC solar) and Bharuch (9 MW wind, 7.2 MW DC solar). A further 5.4 MW wind and 3.6 MW solar at Bharuch are due by December 2026 (S1, p.35, 141, 299-300).

In FY26 the standalone plant met 75.44% of its power from the captive plant. On a combined basis the grid share was 33.02%, against 61.68% in FY24 (S1, p.315-316).

Power and fuel still cost Rs.134.82 crore in FY26 (8.56% of expenses). The sponge-iron kiln is legacy equipment that was only partly refurbished after the 2018 acquisition, and the certifier applies an obsolescence factor to its capacity (S1, p.310, 427).

About the 'Green steel' name: the company's TMT holds a 4-star and the subsidiary's a 5-star green-steel rating from NISST. The certificate dated 15 Sep 2026 is valid only to 31 Mar 2027 (S1, p.297, 167-168). The process is still coal-DRI plus induction furnace, and the 'green' credentials rest on waste-heat recovery, scrap use and renewables.

Sales go through three channels. The mix is shifting from distributors toward dealers, which should reduce dependence on a few large intermediaries. At 31 March 2026 there were 12 distributors (37.57% of FY26 revenue), 148 dealers (20.89%) and 343 direct institutional customers such as roads, engineering, thermal plants and real estate (41.53%) (S1, p.300, 316-318; S11).

Concentration is falling but still high:
- Half of revenue comes from ten customers, and all of the top ten are in Gujarat.
- The FY24 top ten included listed peer VMS TMT (3.00%) and promoter-group company Iraki Enterprise (2.69%) (S1, p.24-26).
- Scrap is mostly imported at spot prices, paid in USD/EUR, mainly from the UAE, US and Singapore. Coal is bought locally but originates in Indonesia and South Africa, and ore is bought domestically on spot terms. There are no long-term supply contracts (S1, p.27-29, 313-315).
- FY26 was the first year with exports, of billets to Tanzania, Sri Lanka and Cape Verde, but only 1.13% of revenue (S1, p.304).

items: JSW One Distribution manufacturing-partner agreement (25 Apr 2025, 3 years): JSW One gives technical support, and the company can make product that JSW One sells under its own brand. No revenue from it is disclosed (S1, p.342-343; S16).
Job work with Hibond Steel (effective 24 May 2026, 3 years): Hibond rolls at least 3,000 t a month of TMT from GGSPL's billets (S1, p.343).

Brand licences: the subsidiary pays about Rs.13.34 lakh a month to Shree Ganesh Rolling Mills and Rs.7.32 lakh a month to Madan Lal Gupta HUF to make 'Jindal' TMT in Gujarat. It also supplies 'ESSAR TMT' under a Stecol agreement running to March 2027 (S1, p.342-343).
Staff: 1,357 employees plus 143 contract workers at March 2026. Attrition was 27.70% in FY26 and 38.66% in FY25 (S1, p.318-322).

blocks.text: The industry report in the offer documents is by CARE Analytics, dated 24 June 2025 in the DRHP. It says India's finished-steel consumption grew from 100 MT in FY20 to 150 MT in FY25, an 8.4% CAGR, with FY25 up 10.2%. CARE projects about 8.2% CAGR to around 206 MT by FY29 (S2, p.197, 234-235). Long products, the category TMT belongs to, grew from 52.2 MT to 76.5 MT between FY19 and FY24, a 7.9% CAGR. TMT consumption was 50.3 MT in FY23 (S2, p.205-206).

The secondary-steel route GGSPL uses (sponge iron plus induction furnace) produced 51.1 MT, or 35.4% of India's crude steel, in FY24. It grew at 9.1% CAGR over FY19-FY24, faster than the blast-furnace route (S2, p.210). Demand is driven by infrastructure and construction: the FY26 central infrastructure allocation was Rs.11.21 lakh crore (S2, p.183, 236). The volume tailwind is real. So is the price cycle: TMT prices were down 0.8-3.1% year on year in March 2025, and average finished-steel prices fell from Rs.84,963/t in FY22 to Rs.65,383/t in FY25 (S2, p.202, 238).

CARE itself flags that Gujarat added 68 new steel units in five years, the most of any state, creating overcapacity that cheap imports make worse. It also notes that logistics put the company at a price disadvantage outside Gujarat (S2, p.242-243). This is the company's home and almost only market.

The offer document's peer set is MSP Steel & Power, Gallantt Ispat, Kamdhenu, VMS TMT and Beekay Steel (S1, p.288-295; S2, p.247-248). Of these, only VMS TMT is a direct Gujarat rival of similar scale. In practice GGSPL also competes with large integrated brands (JSW, Tata Tiscon, SAIL) and dozens of unlisted Gujarat re-rollers (S2, p.242). Operating comparisons are shown below; valuation comparisons are deliberately left out.

blocks.caption: Operating comparison from the CARE report (S2, p.248-253; FY26 revenue from S1 industry section)
rows: 34.1 MW captive (coal 16, WHR 4, hybrid 14.1) at DRHP date

blocks.text: The FY26 comparison in the RHP puts GGSPL's revenue of Rs.1,679 crore below Gallantt (Rs.4,419 crore) and MSP (Rs.2,843 crore), and above Beekay, VMS and Kamdhenu (S1, industry section p.288-295). Note that CARE's peer margin tables appear to have mislabelled columns in both the DRHP and RHP, so treat individual peer margins with caution (S1; S2, p.251).

Plainly, no. The offer document makes no market-share claim, no import-substitution claim and no 'only Indian maker' claim. CARE's strongest statement is that the company is 'among the few players in the region with considerable manufacturing capabilities' (S1, p.288; S2, p.247). On our calculation, 3.02 lakh tonnes of TMT capacity is about 0.6% of the 50.3 MT national TMT market (S2, p.206, 248).

items: Real but replicable advantages: captive coal and waste-heat power plus renewables lower power cost per tonne; DRI-to-TMT integration captures more margin; and the plant is close to Kandla and Mundra ports for imported scrap (S1, p.299-300, 315-316).
Not a moat, because the brand is licensed from a promoter entity and not owned (S1, p.304-305).

Not a moat, because the technology is Thermex quenching licensed from H&K Rolling Mill Engineers on a one-year licence (1 Dec 2025 to 30 Nov 2026), after H&K's cease-and-desist forced the subsidiary to drop the 'TMX' name (S1, p.480-481, 487).
Not a moat, because the product is a BIS-standard commodity (IS 1786) sold on spot purchase orders with no long-term contracts (S1, p.313-318).

blocks.text: Verdict on the moat: GGSPL is a cost-efficient regional commodity producer. It has no structural barrier that protects its margins through a steel-price downcycle.

blocks.caption: Restated consolidated P&L (Rs. crore) (S1, p.298, 391, 453; S6)

blocks.text:
The headline 21.9% revenue CAGR and 38.5% PAT CAGR over FY24-FY26 are real but need unpacking (S1, p.302):
- FY25's 33% jump came mainly from consolidating German TMT (Viramgam) from 21 May 2024. Management itself says average realisation fell 3.61% that year (S1, p.463-464).
- In FY26 the subsidiary alone earned Rs.636.72 crore of revenue and Rs.30.15 crore of PAT (S1, p.435).
- FY26 was the cleaner, mostly organic year: revenue up 11.4% on volume, with EBITDA margin expanding to 9.94% (S1, p.460-463).

Margin drivers in FY26: raw materials plus traded goods fell as a share of revenue as trading shrank (stock-in-trade purchases down 38.67%), and captive power held down energy cost per tonne. Against that, finance cost rose 31.5%, employee cost 29.3% and power and fuel 34.8% (S1, p.460-463). The subsidiary has since recorded no government incentive income: Gujarat IMD incentive was Rs.3.36 crore in FY25 and nil in FY26 (S1, p.452, 460).

blocks.caption: Balance sheet and cash flow (Rs. crore) (S1, p.390, 394, 436, 475; S6)
rows: Free cash flow (CFO minus capex, our calc.)

blocks.text: Operating cash flow was positive in all three years, and in FY26 it exceeded PAT (Rs.140.80 crore vs Rs.79.89 crore), so there is no classic profit-without-cash red flag (S1, p.394). Capex consumed more than the operating cash flow in FY24 and FY25, and the gap was filled with debt, a Rs.32.36 crore rights issue in FY25 and a Rs.49.63 crore pre-IPO placement in September 2025 (S1, p.75, 394).

The main balance-sheet caveat is supplier financing. At March 2026, Rs.242.90 crore of the Rs.329.54 crore in trade payables sat under a supplier-financing arrangement on 0-120 day terms (S1, p.425). That is bank-funded credit which does not appear in the Rs.334.37 crore of reported borrowings. Adding it back roughly doubles effective leverage, and it explains why payable days (about 93 days on purchases, our calculation) are far longer than inventory plus receivable days. The current ratio is 0.97 (S1, p.436).

Other points:
- Inventory days rose from about 41 in FY24 to about 65 in FY26 (our calculation from S1, p.390).
- Receivables older than six months reached Rs.22.0 crore at FY26 (S1, RF14).
- Contingent liabilities total Rs.168.04 crore, including Rs.112.65 crore of income-tax demands (S1, p.83, 468-469).
- Crisil rates the bank facilities A-/Stable and A2+. Its earlier January 2025 rationale cited margin vulnerability to raw-material prices, Gujarat concentration and low value addition as weaknesses (S1, RF8; S14).
- No equity dividend has been paid in the last three years (S1, p.379).

subsections.title: Does the trend support the growth story?

blocks.text:
Partly:
- Volumes are growing and TMT utilisation is high (87.79%). The capex doubles Samakhiyali's rolling and melting capacity, so FY28-FY29 volumes could rise meaningfully if demand holds (S1, p.305, 309).
- But returns on equity have drifted down from 23.67% to 18.86% as equity was raised, and margins remain thin at 4.76% PAT.
- A single steel-price downcycle, like the one that took average prices down about 23% between FY22 and FY25, can erase much of the spread (S1, p.302; S2, p.238).
- The growth story also leans on the acquired subsidiary's earnings. Its purchase from a promoter-family-linked position produced a bargain-purchase capital reserve of Rs.19.96 crore (S1, p.435).

Net read on the financials: this is a solid, improving small-cap steel converter. It is not a compounding franchise, and its leverage is higher than the headline 0.79 debt-to-equity once supplier finance is counted.

blocks.text: The DRHP of June 2025 proposed a Rs.450 crore fresh issue plus a 20 lakh-share OFS (S2, p.132; S17). The RHP cut the fresh issue to Rs.290 crore and halved the OFS. The only reason the RHP gives is a Rs.49.63 crore pre-IPO placement (18.38 lakh shares) allotted on 26 September 2025. That explains only about Rs.50 crore of the Rs.160 crore reduction, and the rest of the cut is not explained (S1, p.75, 102, 137-138).

subsections.title: Objects of the issue in full

blocks.caption: Use of the fresh issue (Rs. crore) (S1, p.138-140)
rows: Samakhiyali expansion plus hybrid wind-solar plant
balance (about 56 before expenses, our calc.; capped at 25%)

blocks.caption: Capex project cost breakdown (Rs. crore) (S1, p.142-166)
rows: Kiln (+82,500 MTPA sponge iron, incl. WHR boiler)
About 60 POs worth Rs.74.66 crore already issued; about Rs.22.41 crore still quoted
Hybrid power plant (5.4 MW wind + 2.5 MW DC solar)

blocks.text: The expansion takes Samakhiyali from 66,000 to about 1,48,500 MTPA of sponge iron, from 2,14,500 to 4,12,500 TPA of billets and from 1,81,500 to 3,46,500 MTPA of TMT. It also adds structural sections, coated bars and a 288 TPD shredder (S1, p.141, 166, 305). Environmental clearance (April 2025) and Gujarat pollution-board consent to establish are in hand. Consent to operate for the new capacity is still to be applied for (S1, p.38, 167-168).

subsections.title: What the objects mean for an investor

items: Good: about 78% of the fresh issue goes into productive capacity, and only about Rs.13.9 crore leaves as OFS money to the promoters (S1, p.138; S6).
Good: the debt repayment is small (Rs.7.70 crore, about 2.5% of fund-based debt) but retires the most expensive loan at 12.85% (S1, p.169-170).

Concern: nobody independent appraised the project. The cost basis is a Detailed Project Report by CARE Analytics, which also wrote the industry report, and CARE Ratings from the same group is the monitoring agency (S1, p.98, 174-175; S2, p.134-136).

Concern: the schedule slipped. The DRHP targeted commercial production in October 2026, the RHP says December 2027, and the project cost rose from Rs.325.21 crore to Rs.348.14 crore (S1, p.166; S2, p.133, 147).

Concern: civil works and the hybrid plant go to KP-group companies. Independent director Indu Rao Kaveti sits on the boards of K.P. Green Engineering and K.P. Energy, and K.P. Energy is also a lessor of the company's power-plant land (S1, p.143, 165, 347-354).
Minor: the RHP notes that lender consent for the IPO was obtained from all lenders except Central Bank of India (S1, p.171).

blocks.text: Offer expenses and the exact net proceeds were blank ([●]) in the RHP pages we read, so general-corporate-purpose money is estimated by subtraction.

The promoters are brothers Inamulhaq Shamsulhaq Iraki (57, Chairman and Whole-time Director) and Abdulhaq Shamsulhaq Iraki (55, Managing Director), plus Inamulhaq's son Ibrarulhaq (31, Whole-time Director, B.Com, IIM-A executive programme). Together they held 81.28% of shares before the offer (S1, p.57, 347-354, 370). The family has been in steel since their father founded Iraki Scrap Suppliers in 1976. The brothers have 30-36 years of trading and manufacturing experience but no formal education, which the RHP lists as a risk factor (S1, p.301, RF57; S16).

blocks.caption: Board and key managers (S1, p.347-369)
rows: FY26 pay Rs.157.5 lakh (Rs.90 lakh in FY25)
Former Joint Commissioner, Gujarat State Tax
Director of K.P. Green Engineering and K.P. Energy (capex vendor and power-land lessor)

blocks.text: The entire independent board apart from one director was appointed in May 2025, weeks before the DRHP. Only one director has previously sat on a listed company's board (S1, p.355-356, RF41). The CS has changed twice in two years, most recently two months before the issue opened (S1, p.367-369; S3). Promoters' pay rose about 75% in FY26 (S1, p.437-441).

This section is not routine. The promoter family runs a cluster of entities on both sides of GGSPL's trade:
- Iraki Enterprise Ltd was an associate until a buyback in June 2024. It is also the second-largest supplier (S1, p.84-88).
- Four group companies (Iraki Enterprise, Haq Steels, Shree Ranisati Ingots, Sunstar Enterprises) are explicitly authorised to carry on a similar line of business. The RHP says they do not currently make sponge iron, billets or TMT (S1, p.375-378, RF38).

items: The receivable from Kaavyaratna LLPs was Rs.20.6 crore at March 2026, against Rs.19.2 crore of sales to them that year. The company also paid one of them a Rs.6.9 crore capital advance. What these LLPs are and why a steel maker advances capital to one is not explained (S1, p.84-88, 437-441).
Premises: the registered office is leased from Iraki Enterprise, and Viramgam land is leased from Haq Steels and Viramgam Rerolling Mills. All three are promoter-linked (S1, p.375-378).
Guarantees: promoters personally guarantee company borrowings and also group-company loans (Iraki Enterprise about Rs.76 crore, Sunstar about Rs.23 crore) without charging a fee (S1, p.344-346).

Subsidiary purchase: German TMT was bought in steps in 2024. The first 5,000 shares came from Abdulhaq's sons at Rs.1,400 a share, and the rest was taken at Rs.10 a share. The deal produced a Rs.19.96 crore bargain-purchase reserve (S1, p.336-340, 435).
Promoter loans to the company are now small (Rs.3.05 crore outstanding at March 2026) and interest-free (S1, p.437-441).

Penalties on 15 Dec 2025 (suo moto adjudication): Rs.1.46 lakh for no woman director, Rs.5 lakh for no audit committee until Feb 2022, Rs.5 lakh for no NRC and Rs.3 lakh for no independent directors. Inamulhaq and Abdulhaq were each fined Rs.1 lakh per breach (S1, RF36).
Late statutory dues (PF, ESI, TDS, GST): 20 instances in FY24, 28 in FY25 and 19 in FY26. Several RoC forms for FY22-FY23 were filed late (S1, RF35).

Income-tax search and seizure, 17-19 Jan 2023, covering the registered office, promoters, group companies and both plants. Demands have been quantified and appeals are pending. Income-tax contingent liability is Rs.112.65 crore (S1, p.63, 83, 451).
Tax cases: company 26 cases (Rs.107.25 crore of the Rs.108.75 crore aggregate); promoters 16 cases (Rs.32.19 crore); subsidiary 2 cases (Rs.13.17 crore) (S1, p.39, 482).

Civil matters: a Paschim Gujarat Vij appeal over electricity billing (about Rs.1.6 crore); the H&K Thermex/TMX trademark dispute, settled by a new licence; and a Supreme Court SLP by Prudent Arc against the company's DRT-auction purchase of the Global Hi-tech Industries plant in Kutch. Rs.23.28 crore was paid; the DRAT ruled in the company's favour, the sale deed was signed on 28 Nov 2025, and the asset now sits in land/CWIP pending the SLP (S1, p.480-481; S3, p.52).
Three workplace fatalities (FY23, FY24, FY26) (S1, RF17).
Previous auditor KPSJ & Associates resigned in November 2023, citing pre-occupation (S1, p.98).
No criminal or SEBI proceedings against the company, promoters or directors (S1, p.39, 479).

blocks.text: Governance read: none of these items is individually fatal. Together, though (a group-wide tax search, a brand owned by the promoters, a dense and growing related-party ring, and a history of running without mandatory committees), they point to a family-run group whose listed entity is not yet clearly ring-fenced from the promoters' other interests.

items: 1. Tax overhang: Rs.112.65 crore of income-tax contingent liabilities, up from nil in FY24 and about 27% of net worth, plus Rs.32.19 crore against the promoters. An adverse appellate outcome would hit both the balance sheet and management bandwidth (S1, p.39, 63, 83).
2. Single-state commodity exposure: 97.74% of sales are in Gujarat, a market CARE calls over-capacitised. TMT prices are cyclical and there are no long-term contracts (S1, p.304, 316; S2, p.242).

3. Execution risk on a capex bigger than the current asset base: the Rs.348 crore project compares with FY26 PPE of Rs.488 crore. It has already slipped about 14 months, is only partly ordered, and was not independently appraised (S1, p.138-168, 390).

4. Hidden leverage and liquidity: Rs.242.90 crore of supplier-financed payables, a current ratio of 0.97, and covenants that restrict dividends, new projects and changes in control (S1, p.425, 436, 476-478).
5. IP dependence on related and third parties: the brand is owned by promoter-group company Haq Steels, and the Thermex technology licence from H&K runs year to year (S1, p.342-343, 487).
6. Raw-material and currency risk: materials are 82.77% of expenses, and 22.43% of purchases are imported and paid in USD/EUR at spot prices (S1, RF3).

7. Related-party and conflict risk: group companies may enter the same business; there are new sales to, receivables from and a capital advance to the Kaavyaratna LLPs; and an independent director is linked to a capex vendor (S1, p.84-88, 347-354, 375-378).
8. People and safety: 38.66% employee attrition in FY25 and 27.70% in FY26, three fatalities in four years, and no key-man or product-liability insurance (S1, RF9, RF17, RF40).

blocks.text: Deliberately left out: generic boilerplate risks the RHP repeats for every issuer (macro, pandemic, FEMA, listing-price volatility).

Some risks are easing, and these are real improvements the investor should credit:
- Customer concentration is falling: top 10 customers went from 57.92% to 50.62% of revenue between FY24 and FY26.
- Supplier concentration is falling: top 10 suppliers went from 53.33% to 41.30% of purchases.
- Import dependence is falling: from 48.96% to 22.43% of purchases (S1, p.24-29).

Monitoring and project costing both sit within the CARE group, so the investor relies on management's delivery with limited independent checks (S1, p.98, 175). The anchor book was small, Rs.91.17 crore from six investors, and the names reported (Necta Bloom, Lords MultiGrowth Fund, Zeal Global Opportunities, Venus Investments) are not large domestic mutual funds (S7). That offers limited institutional validation.

Once listed, the promoters retain about 68.5% (with promoter group) and effectively control all resolutions (S6). The lenders' covenants give banks a say over management and ownership changes (S1, p.476-478).

The offer documents contain no numerical revenue or margin guidance. What management has committed to in writing is the capacity plan and its timetable:
- Civil works October 2026 to April 2027, machinery procurement March to June 2027, trial runs October to November 2027, and commercial production December 2027 (S1, p.166-167).
- The remaining 5.4 MW wind and 3.6 MW solar at Bharuch are due by 31 December 2026 (S1, p.141).
- Management describes the MD&A outlook as seasonal demand with weaker monsoon quarters (S1, p.456-457).

items: Stated strategies (S1, p.304-306): expand into Rajasthan, Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh, possibly using third-party contract manufacturers; grow institutional customers.
Value-added products: cut-and-bend, epoxy/zinc-coated and corrosion-resistant TMT, structural sections, stainless round bars, fly-ash bricks (S1, p.297-306).
Contract manufacturing for JSW One Distribution and job-work rolling through Hibond to add volume without capex (S1, p.342-343).
Brand building, including a recent celebrity endorsement (S1, p.304-306).
The launch press release repeats the capacity targets but gives no forward numbers (S9).

blocks.text: We found no investor call or management interview with concrete forward guidance. Business Standard's launch coverage (22 Sep 2026) only restates the offer's purpose: capacity expansion and renewable power (S19). Any growth trajectory beyond FY26 is therefore an inference from capacity, not a management forecast.

If the expansion is delivered on time and utilisation holds, Samakhiyali's TMT capacity roughly doubles from FY28. The main revenue step-up therefore arrives two years after listing. Meanwhile FY27 results depend on steel prices and on how well the Gujarat market absorbs the added regional capacity (S1, p.166, 305; S2, p.242).

Upside triggers: new states, JSW One volumes, and a green-steel premium if CBAM-type demand for certified low-carbon rebar develops (S2, p.241-245). Downside triggers: a steel-price correction, an adverse tax appeal, or further schedule slippage.

subsections.title: Anchor book, day-1 status and grey market

blocks.text: The anchor round on 24 September 2026 raised Rs.91.17 crore from six institutional investors at the upper end of the band (Rs.139). The largest were Necta Bloom (Rs.30 crore) and Lords MultiGrowth Fund (Rs.20 crore), with Zeal Global Opportunities Fund and Venus Investments among the others (S7). None of the sources we opened reported the anchors' lock-in dates.

blocks.caption: Subscription status as of day 1 (25 Sep 2026) (S13; S8)

blocks.text: This report was written on the opening day. Tracking sites still showed zero or unpublished bids, so there is no meaningful demand signal yet, and the day-1 figure should not be read as weak demand (S13). Full category-wise data will be available only after close on 29 September.

Grey market premium (unofficial, unregulated, not an investment signal): trackers reported a GMP of Rs.28-29 on 24 Sep 2026, up from Rs.15 on 23 Sep (S8; S18). Another site quoted Rs.24 (S15). GMP can reverse quickly and says nothing about the business, so it has no weight in our verdict.

method:
Primary sources, read directly:
- The RHP dated 21 Sep 2026, downloaded from the BRLM Systematix's site (S1).
- The DRHP dated 29 Jun 2025 (S2).
- The cover of the August 2026 addendum (S3), from the company's investor page (S5).

How the prospectus was read: we read these PDFs page by page as page images, not as extracted text, split across parallel readers. RHP sections read: Objects, Risk Factors, Our Business, History, Management, Promoters, Group Companies, the restated FY24-FY26 financial statements (P&L, balance sheet, cash flow, related-party note), MD&A, Financial Indebtedness and Litigation. The DRHP was read for the original offer structure, the FY22-FY24 history and the CARE industry report. Page references (p.x) are printed page numbers.

What comes from secondary sources: final issue terms (price band, lot, fresh vs OFS amounts, post-issue promoter holding), anchor-investor details, day-1 subscription and GMP. These were cross-checked across Chittorgarh, Investorgain, IndiaIPO, Kotak Neo, IPO Guru and IPO Watch. The Business Standard article was blocked (HTTP 403), so it is cited only from search-result text.

Material gaps:
1. Offer expenses and net proceeds were blank in the RHP pages read, so general corporate purposes is estimated by subtraction.
2. Day-1 subscription data had not been published at the time of writing.
3. Anchor lock-in dates were not found in the sources opened.
4. The August 2026 addendum's restated FY24-FY26 financials were read in full and match the RHP. The addendum confirms no auditor qualifications, a single segment, and the Rs.242.90 crore supplier-finance payables.
5. The RHP does not fully explain why the fresh issue was cut from Rs.450 crore to Rs.290 crore.

Discarded data: one aggregator (multibagg) showed PAT figures inconsistent with the RHP, and Groww showed a wrong face value; neither was used.

Calculations: free cash flow, working-capital days and market-share approximations are our own arithmetic from RHP figures and are labelled as such.

Exclusions: valuation (P/E, EV/EBITDA, market-cap multiples and peer multiples) is excluded by design. The pre-IPO placement price was deliberately not used as a valuation signal.
